caption:
Ordering at a Korean restaurant? Just point and say this 👇

이거 하나 주세요 (i-geo ha-na ju-se-yo) = "One of this, please."
이거 두 개 주세요 (i-geo du gae ju-se-yo) = "Two of this, please."

Works for food, drinks, anything you can point at. Save this for your trip 🍲

At a Korean convenience store, they'll ask if you need a bag. Say this 👇

봉투는 괜찮아요 (bong-tu-neun gwen-cha-na-yo)
= "I don't need a bag, thanks."

Need one instead? 봉투 주세요 (bong-tu ju-se-yo).
Save this for your trip 🏪

On the Seoul subway and not sure about the train? Ask this. 👇

이거 홍대 가요? (i-geo hong-dae ga-yo?)
= "Does this go to Hongdae?"

For the bus too: 이 버스 명동 가요?

Ordering coffee in Korea? Say this. 👇

아이스 아메리카노 하나 주세요 (a-i-seu a-me-ri-ka-no ha-na ju-se-yo)
= "One iced americano, please."

Hot one? 따뜻한 아메리카노 주세요

Paying at a small shop in Korea? Ask this first. 👇

카드 돼요? (ka-deu dwae-yo?)
= "Can I pay by card?"

Cash only? They'll say 현금만 돼요

Need the restroom in Korea? Say this. 👇

화장실 어디예요? (hwa-jang-sil eo-di-ye-yo?)
= "Where is the restroom?"

Swap the place: 출구 어디예요? (where's the exit?)

Can't handle spicy food? Say this when you order. 👇

안 맵게 해 주세요 (an maep-ge hae ju-se-yo)
= "Not spicy, please."

A little spicy is ok: 조금만 맵게 해 주세요
